themes.title: Lilly agrees to acquire Merida Biosciences for up to $2.875B — its 13th deal of 2026
themes.description: Announced Aug 31, the deal targets Merida's autoantibody-degrader biologics, led by MER511 for Graves' disease and thyroid eye disease, with the transaction expected to close in Q4 2026. It isn't an AI-discovery deal, but it shows the cash Lilly's obesity franchise keeps throwing off into an aggressive bolt-on M&A pace — 13 acquisitions in eight months — alongside its AI partnerships (Isomorphic, NVIDIA, Insilico) and its owned in-vivo editing asset, Verve.

themes.tag: SENTIMENT COOLS FASTER THAN THE SCIENCE
themes.title: Generate Biomedicines slides to $16.39, giving back most of its Aug 25 all-time-high gain
themes.description: GENB hit an all-time high of $20.38 on Aug 25 after its Q2 print and GB-0895 Phase 3 progress, then slid back to $16.39 within two weeks — still above the $16 IPO price but a sharp round trip on no negative news. GB-0895 remains in global Phase 3 (SOLAIRIA-1/2, live in 33 of a planned 42 countries) and Generate is presenting three posters on it at the European Respiratory Society Congress this week (Sept 5-9). The clinical story hasn't moved; the stock's enthusiasm has.

themes.title: Eli Lilly enters ARKG's top 10 as Illumina slips and ARK trims Tempus AI, Twist Bioscience
themes.description: In this week's holdings snapshot (Sept 2), Eli Lilly's ARKG weight rose enough to crack the top 10 at #10 (3.90%, up from 3.72% and #11 last week), displacing CareDx, while Illumina slipped from #7 to #9 (3.95%, down from 4.08%). Separately, ARK trimmed Twist Bioscience (~$1.58M) and Tempus AI (~$1.3M) through ARKK while continuing to add to Intellia Therapeutics across both ARKK and ARKG (~$395K) — a rotation, not a clean sector call, with Intellia's rolling BLA for lonvo-z the fundamental story behind the buying.

themes.tag: THE TOOLING LAYER SPLITS IN TWO DIRECTIONS
themes.title: Quantum-Si confirms a second Proteus delay and a 20% workforce cut while 908 Devices gets a Stifel upgrade
themes.description: Quantum-Si confirmed the Proteus protein-sequencer launch has slipped to Q2 2027 — a full year late — and is cutting 20% of its workforce to save ~$12M annually and extend its cash runway into Q4 2028. On the same week, Stifel raised its 908 Devices price target to $12 (from $10, Buy) after a Q2 beat (revenue +23% y/y to $16.1M). Same multiomics instrument layer, opposite trajectories — a reminder that the tooling thesis doesn't move as one block.

private_watchlist.name: Isomorphic Labs
private_watchlist.note: AlphaFold 3 lineage; Thrive Capital-led round adds MGX, Temasek, CapitalG & UK Sovereign AI Fund alongside Alphabet/GV. ISM8969 cleared FDA for human trials Jan 28, 2026 — the oncology candidate CEO Demis Hassabis says will anchor Isomorphic's first clinical trials by year-end 2026, a year later than his original 2025 target. No fresh update this week; the delayed timeline remains the operative fact, and being Alphabet-owned makes a near-term IPO unlikely regardless.

private_watchlist.name: Insilico Medicine
private_watchlist.note: Formally initiated the Phase III GENESIS-IPF trial for rentosertib on Jul 7, 2026 — 320 patients, 52 weeks, 47 centers across China; the Phase IIa data behind it (published in Nature Medicine) showed +98.4 mL forced vital capacity improvement at 12 weeks on the 60mg arm. No fresh disclosure this week; still the field's clearest clinical proof point and the only name here already public (HKEX, Dec 2025, $292M IPO).

private_watchlist.name: Xaira Therapeutics
private_watchlist.note: Launched X-Cell, its first virtual cell model (4.9B parameters, trained on the 25.6M-cell X-Atlas/Pisces dataset), in March 2026. Built out its clinical leadership over the summer — Ci Chu to Chief Discovery Officer, Bo Wang to Chief AI Scientist, Rachel Lane as SVP Business Development & Operations — continuing the shift from platform-building toward actually running trials, though no trial has started yet.

private_watchlist.name: NewLimit
private_watchlist.note: Epigenetic reprogramming for longevity (Founders Fund, Lilly Ventures, Jun 2026); moved its first candidate medicine into large-scale manufacturing in January, still targeting clinical entry as early as 2027. NewLimit alone accounts for roughly 71% of this year's disclosed longevity funding (~$614M through August) — the sector's capital is concentrating hard in cellular reprogramming, with Retro Biosciences (Sam Altman-backed, ~$1.8B pre-money, $1.18B+ cumulative raised) reportedly still working to close a further ~$1B round.

bear_case.title: Biology still fails in the clinic — and this week's best news is still early
bear_case.description: Zero AI-discovered drugs have reached full FDA approval. Recursion's TUPELO data, Generate's Phase 3 entry and Lilly's VERVE-102 durability are all genuine progress — but they're Phase 1-3 readouts, not approvals, and the field's clearest recent clinical win (Intellia's HAELO, now a rolling BLA) still isn't an AI-discovery story.

bear_case.title: IP litigation is now a multi-year balance-sheet risk, not a footnote
bear_case.description: Guardant Health has formally appealed the $245.2M TwinStrand judgment to the Federal Circuit while separately pursuing PTAB challenges to the underlying patents — two parallel tracks that could run for years, even with execution stayed in the meantime. Its own offensive suit against Tempus still has a Markman hearing pending Oct 20. Patent risk cuts in both directions in the diagnostics layer, and it moves real money either way.

bear_case.title: Catalyst-driven volatility, in both directions
bear_case.description: Generate Biomedicines rallied to an Aug 25 all-time high of $20.38, then gave back most of that move to sit at $16.39 barely a week and a half later — with no change to the underlying GB-0895 Phase 3 program either way. Relay has cooled off its own highs too. Proof these stocks can re-rate violently on sentiment and single data points alone, detached from the clinical facts — in a portfolio, that volatility cuts both ways.

bear_case.title: Hardware and instrument risk isn't just a biology problem
bear_case.description: Quantum-Si confirmed the Proteus launch is now a full year late (pushed to Q2 2027) and is cutting 20% of its workforce to fund the delay, extending cash runway to Q4 2028 — buying time, but not shipping the product. Compare that to Abbott's ~$21B all-cash purchase of Exact Sciences: real test volumes and reimbursed CPT codes command real M&A premiums, while unproven instrument platforms carry genuine execution risk regardless of the underlying science.

bear_case.title: Funding is recovering, but selectively
bear_case.description: H1 2026 venture funding reached $16.3B across 235 rounds and M&A already topped all of 2025 — but roughly two-thirds of those venture rounds still went to biotechs that already had a drug in human testing. Early-formation platforms remain comparatively starved of capital even as headline totals hit multi-year highs, and long-duration rate sensitivity can close the funding window unevenly.

positions.name: Eli Lilly

positions.name: Novartis

positions.name: NVIDIA
